messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: unexpected expressions in dplyr select
parts:
I was playing with select() and discovered that select(mtcars,disp+hp) simply adds the indices of those columns and returns the 7th column as a result.

Is that really an example of something that is an intended use of the evaluation of the column names, or might it be better for that to throw an error?

(It would be neat if select(mtcars,disp + hp) returned the sum of the columns, but I'm guessing that's not the intended use for select())

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: unexpected expressions in dplyr select
parts:
All of the dplyr verb use non-standard evaluation, so it's possible to
break them all with a little work. I'm happy with the current trade
off in select() - converting column names to numeric indices is nice
because then : and - have a trivial implementation.

OTOH, changing the implementation to use custom : and - functions
inside of select would have the advantage of making richer selection
operations (e.g. https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/issues/158) easier to
implement. I'll keep thinking about it.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: unexpected expressions in dplyr select
parts:
My vote is for throwing an error, for the benefit of idiots like me.  Even after reading the manual, I don't think any user could anticipate what this code would do:

t %>% dplyr::select(id, z = log(y))

It returns z equal to the first column of t, regardless of the value of y, and even if y is NA.
